sb_prompt: PLEASE DISCUSS MUSIC.  CAN YOU FIND MUSICIANSOR TYPES OF MUSIC THAT BOTH YOU AND THE OTHER CALLER LIKE?
turns: So, why do you like music? Did you always like it or did you start later?
I've always loved it, honestly, but I'm weirdly conflicted about the whole industry now.

Oh, yeah? That's rough, I get that a lot sometimes. Like, when you think about how many people in this business are just selling out or something, it's kind of depressing. But I still love it myself. Do you like any specific genres, or is it mostly just the classics for you?

Yeah, it's pretty jarring actually, especially when you think about the fact that a girl I went to school with is in that exact situation and she just seems so drained, but honestly, I still can't turn off the stuff I actually like, like jazz or indie folk, which sounds weird coming from someone who works with antibiotics every day.

Oh wow, that is really heavy, and honestly? That sounds like exactly what I've been feeling lately too, even though I'm not actually in the industry at all, I just... decided I wanted to be in it years ago and I just can't quite figure out why I stuck with it when everyone else seems to be running away. Do you listen to that jazz or folk stuff when you're off the clock, or is it just for work breaks?

Off the clock? Oh yeah, mostly that. Like, I'll put on some Joni Mitchell while I'm making pills and it just hits different than the pop stuff I have to listen to in the car. It helps me feel like I'm somewhere else when I'm surrounded by germs and broken bones.

That actually makes perfect sense, because honestly I feel that exact same pull when I'm standing on a cold street trying to close a deal and I just need something that feels real rather than just polished for the radio. Do you ever find yourself really zoning out to the jazz stuff, or do you have to consciously focus on the lyrics to keep from checking your phone?
Honestly, I usually just close my eyes and let the notes wash over me, but I gotta be careful not to zone out too much or I'll forget to check the dosage before I hand out the meds.

That's actually a really good safety net, and I totally respect that, because I never let myself get that absorbed in the details when I'm out showing houses, which is probably why I'm usually just humming along to whatever's on the playlist without really thinking about it.
Yeah, I guess I'm lucky I don't sell houses, because if I ever forgot to check the dosage, that would be way more dangerous than forgetting to dial into the third verse.

Yeah, totally, you're right to be careful, but honestly the house hunting stuff is usually just so chaotic and loud that by the time I get home I need something to just fill the silence without it being too heavy on the brain.
Yeah, that sounds nice, but sometimes I just grab a quick track on the commute so I don't have to unpack anything complex before my shift ends.
That sounds smart, definitely better than trying to unpack a whole album before you have to start your day, especially if you're just trying to get through the commute without a headache.
Yeah, I get that, usually I just hum the chorus and try not to think too hard about what I'm actually doing.
Yeah, that's exactly how I feel about the commute, usually I just let it wash over me so I don't have to carry anything heavy into the next showing.
Yeah, it's nice not to have to unpack anything before you even step through the door.
Yeah, that's probably the best way to keep the brain in the car, honestly.
Yeah, exactly, it's like hitting a reset button before you even walk through the front door.
Yeah, that reset button is definitely what I'm looking for, I don't wanna drag any heavy stuff from the street into my apartment.
Yeah, that's the thing, music just needs to be a clean slate so I can actually focus on the patients when I walk in.
Yeah, I get that, I just need something to wipe the floor clean so I can walk into the next showing without carrying any of that street chaos with me.
Exactly, I need that mental wipe so I can actually focus on the patients when I walk in.
Yeah, that's exactly what I'm looking for, something light enough to just float in without making me think too hard before I meet the next buyer.
Yeah, that's exactly what I need, just something light enough to float in so I don't drag any of that stress into the clinic.
That actually helps a lot, honestly, knowing you can just swap genres instantly depending on whether I need to be distracted or focused.
Yeah, it's nice that you can switch that easily, though sometimes I feel like I'm just listening to one side of the coin and never really get to hear the music itself anymore.

Yeah, I totally get the "one side of the coin" thing, because honestly, sometimes it feels like the music just stops being music and starts being white noise for survival, but I do think there are moments when it actually does hit differently, maybe if I just slowed down the pace a little. Do you ever find a song or an artist that breaks through that filter?

Yeah, there's this indie folk band I used to go to school with that plays really acoustic stuff, and hearing them live last week totally broke the spell for a little bit, it was actually really healing to just see her play without the pressure.
That's actually really powerful, it must feel good to see her playing without the business pressure crushing her down.
Yeah, it's wild to see her play like that when she's barely speaking a word, like the music is the only thing that still makes sense to her.
Yeah, that sounds really freeing, it's wild to see her perform like that when she's barely even talking.

Yeah, she just kind of stood there with her acoustic guitar and started singing, and for like three minutes it was just her voice and the room, no business talk or nothing, and honestly it was the most honest thing I've heard her do in years.
That's actually really touching, honestly, because even though I haven't had that exact situation yet, I think everyone kind of needs those quiet moments sometimes.
Yeah, it was just her and the room, no phones, no pitch stuff, and for a minute it felt like we were all just breathing together instead of selling or buying anything.
That really hits different when you're just breathing without selling anything, honestly.
Yeah, it's wild how fast that silence can make you feel real again, even if it only lasts a minute.
Yeah, that silence is kind of rare, so I think I'm just gonna let it sit there for a minute and not say anything else.
Yeah, I think I'm gonna leave it at that, maybe I'll just hum something soft on the way to the clinic.
Yeah, maybe I'll just hum something soft on the way to my next showing.
Yeah, maybe I'll just hum something soft on the way to the clinic.
